free_text_notes.physician_note: 81-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, admitted 6/15 with new-onset heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Transitioned from IV to oral diuretic yesterday; weight stable. A skin integrity check was performed on admission as per standard protocol. No pressure sores or skin concerns were identified during the stay. The patient mentioned they have a long-standing dislike of hospitals and was keen to leave as soon as possible. They were reassured and all discharge steps were completed on schedule.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Slept well overnight. Voiding without difficulty. Discharge paperwork still waiting on the summary.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: Met with patient and sister to review the discharge plan. 6/17 17:00: Furosemide changed from 20 mg daily to 40 mg daily on evening rounds. Patient and sister not yet told; this afternoon's teaching covered the old dose.
